messages:
anya: Customer reported streaming responses truncating mid-message and client reconnect loops. Happens after ~55-65s of no new bytes. They pasted a transcript where the model response stops mid-sentence and the client sees a TCP FIN, then reconnects and gets a fresh 200 but no resume. Request ID: req_0a1b2c, trace: trace-9f8e

anya: Repro steps I used locally:
```
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true'
```
Response: first few tokens streamed, then nothing, connection closed by peer. Server logs show last write at t=55s then connection reset at t=62s.

devon: Does this customer sit behind any CDN or LB? ALB / Cloudflare / nginx?

anya: They have Cloudflare in front of an ALB that routes to our fleet (nginx proxy -> app). Region-specific: EU edge uses Cloudflare, US sometimes directly ALB.

kevin: Sounds like classic idle-timeout + buffering interaction. ALB default idle timeout is 60s (it will close if no bytes are transferred). Cloudflare also tends to buffer responses in some modes (and will close if upstream stalls). Two vectors: backend/app not consistently sending heartbeats OR intermediate proxies are buffering so the ALB doesn't see continuous small writes.

anya: Logs show the app calls flush() after each token. But nginx had gzip on and proxy_buffering likely enabled. Suspect buffering at nginx or Cloudflare.

devon: Can you try reproducing with proxy buffering disabled in our staging nginx? Quick nginx snippet to disable buffering for streaming endpoints:
```
location /v1/generate {
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
}
```
Note: `proxy_set_header Connection "";` avoids `Connection: close` being added. Also make sure `gzip off;` for that location to prevent nginx from waiting for a full buffer.

kevin: For ALB/ELB specifically, either (A) have the backend send periodic heartbeats so bytes flow and ALB doesn't hit idle timeout, or (B) raise the ALB idle timeout to e.g. 180s. Cloudflare: if customer relies on Cloudflare's proxying, CF may buffer by default — streaming reliably through CF sometimes requires Cloudflare Workers or the "stream" feature, otherwise it aggregates.

anya: Quick mitigation I suggested to customer: implement SSE-style comment pings (send ":\n\n" every 10-15s) so there's consistent wire activity, and ask infra to try disabling buffering + increase ALB idle timeout.

sophie: Any billing/auth impact? They mentioned an auth 401 once in the transcript.

anya: That 401 was a separate call during reconnect and was due to client using expired token; not tied to streaming truncation. Billing unaffected.

kevin: For Envoy users, ensure upstream http1 settings allow chunked transfer encoding and that `use_remote_address`/`idle_timeout` are configured. Example Envoy snippet: `upstream_http_protocol_options: { use_http1: true, idle_timeout: 0s }` and `stream_idle_timeout` settings depending on config. Also disable `proxy_buffering` equivalents.

devon: Repro plan: I'll stand up a staging ALB + nginx + Cloudflare worker to replicate. If I can reproduce, I'll push a small patch to service to emit a lightweight heartbeat (SSE comment) if no tokens produced for >8s.

anya: Customer asked for ETA — can we offer a short-term actionable workaround?

kevin: Short-term: 1) Ask them to bypass Cloudflare (temporarily) to see if issue goes away. 2) Ensure nginx has `proxy_buffering off` and `gzip off` for streaming route. 3) If they control ALB, increase idle timeout to 180s. 4) Implement client reconnect logic that supports `Last-Event-ID` / `Range` style resume (if supported) — otherwise best-effort restart.

support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-184112 and tagged @kevin @devon.

devon: I'll report back with repro + PR link. Expected: small infra change + a 1-line app heartbeat in 1-2 days.

anya: I'll send the customer the short-term checklist and attach the curl repro and headers to try.

kevin: One more note — Cloudflare will sometimes coalesce tiny chunks into a single packet until they reach a certain size or a time threshold; so even if the app is sending token-by-token, CF might not flush immediately. That makes heartbeats crucial if CF is in the path.

anya: Thanks — adding our suggested nginx/ALB/heartbeat steps to the ticket and marking P1 until repro is confirmed in staging.
